BURHAN:v2p129/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.claim: The Prophet supported his descriptions of Paradise with verses: unseen delights by 32:17, the promise to work by the verses of al-Layl, and the tree's long shade by 56:30.
BURHAN:v2p129/r2.anchor: منها حين ذكر ما أعد الله تعالى لأوليائه فى الجنة فقال فيها ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر

QASHANI:92:8-12/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:8-12/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:8-12/r3.claim: Being prepared for hardship is divine abandonment to a downward path from human nature into the abyss of nature, with desires frustrated.
QASHANI:92:8-12/r3.anchor: بالخذلان للطريقة العسرى التي هي الانحطاط عن رتبة الفطرة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.claim: Verses 8–10 describe the character and belief that lead a person to doom and Hell.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r5.anchor: Mentioned in these verses are the character and ideology of a person which lead him to doom and to the pit of Hell.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.claim: Those who treat worldly life as ultimate are miserly, heedless of the Hereafter, and lack resolve for its reward; God lets them pursue their chosen way toward hardship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p348/r5.anchor: They are misers and callously guard their wealth and have no fear of the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.claim: God leaves people without courage for virtue to their base desires; they may seem to progress smoothly until death, then face the steep hardship of 74:17.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r1.anchor: they reach the end of their lives

QIRAAT-ER:92:10:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:92:10:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:92:10:2#1/r1.claim: The standard reading uses the Form II imperfect.
QIRAAT-ER:92:10:2#1/r1.anchor: Standard reading with Form II imperfect

QIRAAT-ER:92:10:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:92:10:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:92:10:4#1/r1.claim: Adding damma on sīn gives fuller vocalization of the same noun pattern.
QIRAAT-ER:92:10:4#1/r1.anchor: Vowel change: ʿusrā → ʿusurā — additional damma on sin, fuller vocalization of the same noun pattern

TUSTARI:92:10-11/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:10-11/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:92:10-11/r1.claim: God makes the hard path easy by enabling the person to perform the deeds of Hell; his wealth cannot help when he falls into it.
TUSTARI:92:10-11/r1.anchor: أي نسهل عليه العمل، بعمل أهل النار، ألا تراه كيف قال عقبه:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.claim: The surah explains which traits bring the success and failure just mentioned in the previous surah, then warns of the Fire and distinguishes those entering it from those spared.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p491/r2.anchor: ولما ذكر فيما قبلها قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها ، ذكر هنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God withholds favors so obedience becomes hardest, or that the easy and difficult are the paths to Paradise and Hell.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r2.anchor: فسنخذله ونمنعه الألطاف حتى تكون الطاعة أعسر شيء عليه وأشد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r3.claim: The author calls a Muʿtazilite implication in al-Zamakhsharī's account and says taysīr can mean preparation for either outcome by way of contrast.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r3.anchor: وفي أول كلامه دسيسة الاعتزال. وجاء فسنيسره للعسرى على سبيل المقابلة

FARRA:v3p270/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p270/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p270/r7.claim: The person is created for misery and barred from good; making the hard path easy is an idiom comparable to warning someone of a blazing Fire.
FARRA:v3p270/r7.anchor: وقوله: فسنيسره للعسرى (10) . يقول: قد خلق على أنه شقي ممنوع من الخير،

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r1.claim: God prepares the miser for the trait leading to hardship and the Fire; yusra and ʿusra are figurative descriptions, and taysīr here means preparation.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r1.anchor: أي للخصلة المؤدية إلى العسر والشدة كدخول النار ومباديه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r2.claim: The future particle sa may emphasize the promise or indicate that most of the promised requital lies in the still-future afterlife.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r2.anchor: قيل للتأكيد وقيل للدلالة على أن الجزاء الموعود معظمه يكون في الآخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r3.speaker: الإرشاد
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r3.claim: Al-Irshad explains why giving and withholding open the two clauses: each is foundational for the later belief, piety, denial, or self-sufficiency.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r3.anchor: في الإرشاد لعل تصدير القسمين بالإعطاء والبخل

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r4.claim: One interpretation takes the first taysir as divine grace and the second as abandonment of grace, with obedience easy for the pious but difficult for others; this is linked to 6:125.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r4.anchor: وقيل التيسير أولا بمعنى اللطف وثانيا بمعنى الخذلان

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r5.claim: Other readings take yusra/usra as paths to Paradise and Hell with taysir meaning guidance, or as obedience and sin and preparation for their beginnings; the latter is a sound, closely related alternative.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r5.anchor: وجوز أن يراد باليسرى طريق الجنة وبالعسرى طريق النار

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r6.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r6.claim: In a report from Ali, the Prophet says everyone's place in Paradise and Fire has been written, but commands them to act because each person is facilitated for the deeds for which they were created, then recites these verses.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r6.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال كنا مع رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r7.claim: The Prophet's instruction is to do the duties of servanthood and leave hidden divine matters to God; the descriptions apply generally despite specific occasions, since the general wording governs while those named are certainly included.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p149#3/r7.anchor: عليكم شأن العبودية وما خلقتم لأجله وأمرتم به وكلوا أمور الربوبية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r3.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r3.claim: Muqatil says God makes it difficult for that person to do good.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: نعسر عليه أن يأتي خيرا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r4.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r4.claim: The Prophet says every soul has a written place in Paradise or Hell, but people must still act: each is eased toward the deeds for which they were created.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r4.anchor: وروينا عن علي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ما من نفس منفوسة إلا [كتب الله] (1) مكانها من الجنة أو النار"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r5.claim: One account says the passage was revealed about Abu Bakr buying Bilal from Umayya for a cloak and ten awqiya, then freeing him; it contrasts their efforts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p446/r5.anchor: قيل: نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق اشترى بلالا من أمية بن خلف ببردة وعشرة أواق، فأعتقه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.claim: In this story, the giver is Abu al-Dahdah, the promised good is reward, and the easier path is Paradise; the miser is the Ansari, who denies reward and is eased toward Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447/r2.anchor: {وأما من بخل واستغنى} يعني الأنصاري، {وكذب بالحسنى} يعني الثواب، {فسنيسره للعسرى} يعني النار.

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r3.claim: God prepares him for a difficult trait leading to hardship, such as entry into Hell.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:8-12/r3.anchor: { فسنيسره للعسرى } للخلة المؤدية إلى العسر والشدة كدخول النار

BINTSHATI:v2p108/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the paths are called easy and hard for their outcomes, or they mean the routes to Paradise and Hell.
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r2.anchor: سمى طريقة الخير باليسرى لأن عاقبتها اليسر

BINTSHATI:v2p108/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r4.claim: Usra appears in this form only in al-Layl; Quranic uses of usr and its derivatives connect hardship to the Day of Resurrection.
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r4.anchor: أما العسرى فلم تأت بهذه الصيغة

BINTSHATI:v2p108/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r5.claim: The author rejects the claim that al-usra was chosen just to preserve the rhyme, and reports al-Zamakhshari's account of God's withholding help as a Mu'tazilite insinuation noted by Abu Hayyan.
BINTSHATI:v2p108/r5.anchor: فما يجوز في البيان العالي التعلق بملحظ شكل في اللفظ

BINTSHATI:v2p109/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r1.claim: Unlike the verbal nouns usr and yusr, usra and yusra convey the extreme of hardship or ease, as do Quranic forms such as the greatest seizure and the greatest Fire.
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r1.anchor: وإنما الملحوظ فيهما، بصيغة الفعلى، أقصى اليسر وأشد العسر

BINTSHATI:v2p109/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r2.claim: Making the most difficult way easy is emphatic warning, comparable to the Quran's ironic announcement of painful punishment for hoarders and other opponents.
BINTSHATI:v2p109/r2.anchor: كالتيسير للعسرى: مبالغة في الردع والنذير لمن بخل واستغنى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r6.claim: God prepares the denier for the hardest, most wretched path: deeds that incur divine anger and lead to Hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r6.anchor: للعسرى * } أي للخصلة التي هي أعسر الأشياء وأنكدها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r8.speaker: النبي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r8.claim: The Prophet’s maxim says each person is made easy for the path for which he was created, supporting the prior decree of each outcome.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p447/r8.anchor: وكما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم - ميسر لما خلق له

NAHHAS:v5p241/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r13.speaker: الضحاك
NAHHAS:v5p241/r13.claim: He interprets al-ʿusrā as the Fire.

NAHHAS:v5p241/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p241/r14.claim: Although facilitation normally concerns good, it can be used for evil like ‘give them glad tidings of painful punishment’; Sibawayh's poem likewise calls a painful beating a greeting.
NAHHAS:v5p241/r14.anchor: أي اجعل ما يقوم لهم مقام البشارة

NAHHAS:v5p241/r15.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p241/r15.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p241/r15.claim: He says that when good is called glad tidings, evil may be described by the corresponding expression.
NAHHAS:v5p241/r15.anchor: هذا قول البصريين وقول الفراء إنه إذا اجتمع خير وشر فوقع للخير تبشير جاز أن يقع للشر مثله

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.claim: He reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal for God; the verses contrast their efforts with those of Umayya and Ubayy, identify the good as the testimony of faith, and the hard path as Hell.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ وابن عساكر عن ابن مسعود

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.claim: Giving means giving from one's bounty and fearing God; the good promise is God's compensation, ease is good, and the opposite is withholding wealth, self-sufficiency, denial, and ease toward evil.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r6.anchor: وأخرج سعيد بن منصور وعبد بن حميد وابن المنذر وابن أبي حاتم وابن جرير والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.claim: He said the giver pays God's due, avoids prohibitions, and believes God's promise; the miser withholds that due, feels self-sufficient, and denies the promise.
DURR-FULL:v8p534/r7.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن أبي حاتم عن قتادة

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي صالح
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.claim: In a report through al-Kalbi and Abu Salih, the giver and God-fearing person is Abu Bakr, while the miser who feels self-sufficient and denies the good is Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r4.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن مردويه وابن عساكر في طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.claim: The Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Fire is written, but commanded people to act: each is made ready for the deeds of the saved or the wretched, then recited this passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r5.anchor: وأخرج أحمد وعبد بن حميد والبخاري ومسلم وأبو داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجة وابن مردويه وابن جرير عن علي بن أبي طالب

DURR-FULL:v8p535/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r6.claim: After the decree in 54:49 was revealed, a man asked whether deeds begin anew or are already settled; the Prophet replied to act, since each is made ready for the easy or hard path.
DURR-FULL:v8p535/r6.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي

DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.claim: Suraqa asked whether deeds were predetermined; the Prophet affirmed the decree but urged action, since each person is eased toward what he was created for, then recited the passage.
DURR-FULL:v8p537/r2.anchor: وأخرج أحمد ومسلم وابن حبان والطبراني وابن مردويه عن جابر بن عبد الله

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas links the sura's revelation to a sale: a stingy palm owner deprived a poor household of fallen dates, then a believer traded forty palms for the tree and gave it to the family; the buyer received a promised palm in Paradise.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3439/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : ان رجلا كان له نخل ومنها نخلة فرعها إلى دار رجل صالح فقير ذي عيال

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the miser withholds wealth, relies on himself, denies God's replacement, and is eased toward evil.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3440#4/r2.anchor: واما من بخل واستغنى قال : بخل بماله واستغنى عن ربه وكذب بالحسنى قال : الخلف من الله فسنيسره للعسرى قال : للشر من الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r5.claim: Taysīr means making something easy to obtain; the direct object is what becomes easy, while the following prepositional phrase identifies the beneficiary, as in the cited verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p382/r5.anchor: والتيسير : جعل شيء يسير الحصول ، ومفعول فعل التيسير هو الشيء الذي يجعل يسيرا ، أي غير شديد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r2.claim: العسرى can denote a state of hardship or punishment, or Hell as a place of severe difficulty; the cited verse calls the Day grievous for unbelievers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r2.anchor: والعسرى : إما الحالة وهي حالة العسر والشدة ، أي العذاب ، وإما مكانته وهي جهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r3.claim: He explains facilitation as leading people into acts of happiness or misery: righteous acts are called easy and evil acts hard according to their eventual outcome for the person.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r3.anchor: وبه فسر ابن عطية ، فالأعمال اليسرى هي الصالحة ، وصفت باليسرى باعتبار عاقبتها لصاحبها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r4.claim: The future marker can signal continuation from now to life's end, and the definite articles in اليسرى and العسرى may mark a kind or something already known.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r4.anchor: وحرف التنفيس على هذا التفسير يكون مرادا منه الاستمرار من الآن إلى آخر الحياة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r5.claim: Because the syntax makes the person the one facilitated and the easy or hard outcome the beneficiary, two analyses are possible; the first preserves the literal verb through rhetorical inversion, intensifying the facilitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p383/r5.anchor: تعين تأويل نظم الآية بإحدى طريقتين : الأولى : إيفاء فعل ( نيسر ) على حقيقته وجعل الكلام جاريا على خلاف مقتضى الظاهر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r1.claim: The second analysis uses تيسير figuratively for preparation and uses the لام for purpose: God prepares people for Paradise or Hell, understood as proper names, by hastening their entry; the phrase for Hell is a mocking parallel to the one for Paradise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r1.anchor: والثانية : أن يكون التيسير مستعملا مجازا مرسلا في التهيئة والإعداد بعلاقة اللزوم بين إعداد الشيء للشيء وتيسره له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r2.claim: Since the described acts precede the promised facilitation, it refers to continuing and increasing those established deeds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r2.anchor: فالأعمال سابقة لا محالة . والتيسير مستقبل بعد حصولها فهو تيسير ما زاد على حصولها ، أي تيسير الدوام عليها والاستزادة منها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r3.claim: Another reading keeps the verb literal and treats easy and difficult as descriptions of a state; facilitation means persisting in action, supported by the Bukhārī report that each person is facilitated toward the work for which they were created and the Prophet then recited these verses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p384/r3.anchor: ففي ( صحيح البخاري ) عن علي قال : ( كنا مع رسول الله في بقيع الغرقد في جنازة فقال : ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد كتب مقعده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r1.claim: The hadith's opening statement that each person's destination was written is not the point of these verses; writing represents God's exact knowledge, and the question about whether to rely on that knowledge is answered by saying good deeds signal a good end.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r1.anchor: جعلت الكتابة تمثيلا لعلم الله بالمعلومات علما موافقا لما سيكون لا زيادة فيه ولا نقص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r2.claim: The verse is connected to the Prophet's recitation as an explanation of فسنيسره: God enables a person to do works of felicity or misery, whether foundational faith or further deeds, and either sense supports divine facilitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r2.anchor: فالذي يرتبط بالآية من اللفظ النبوي هو أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أعقب كلامه بأن قرأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r3.claim: Alternatively, the recitation supports the command to act: deeds mark the person's facilitation, with easy outcomes meaning felicity and Paradise and difficult outcomes meaning misery and the Fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p385/r3.anchor: أو يكون المقصود من سوق الآية الاستدلال على قوله : ( اعملوا ) لأن الآية ذكرت عملا وذكرت تيسيرا لليسرى وتيسيرا للعسرى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p386/r3.claim: The passage uses الجمع مع التقسيم and four antitheses: giving versus withholding, piety versus self-sufficiency, affirmation versus denial, and ease versus hardship.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#3/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#3/r2.claim: Alternatively, it means evil: God prepares the person for evil, leading to the difficult outcome of Hell.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p150#3/r2.anchor: والثاني الشر قاله ابن عباس والمعنى سنهيؤه للشر فيؤديه إلى الأمر العسير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r5.claim: Being facilitated toward hardship means being set on an evil path, as in the verse about hearts and sight being turned away.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r5.anchor: أي: لطريق الشر، كما قال تعالى: {ونقلب أفئدتهم وأبصارهم كما لم يؤمنوا به أول مرة ونذرهم في طغيانهم يعمهون}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r6.claim: Many verses and reports show God grants success to whoever intends good and abandons whoever intends evil, while all occurs by a determined decree.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r6.anchor: والآيات في هذا المعنى كثيرة دالة على أن الله، عز وجل، يجازي من قصد الخير بالتوفيق له،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r7.claim: When Abu Bakr asks whether deeds follow a settled decree or a new decision, the Prophet replies that each person is made ready for what he was created to do.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p417#2/r7.anchor: قلت لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يا رسول الله، أنعمل على ما فرغ منه أو على أمر مؤتنف؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r1.claim: The Prophet says each persons place in Paradise or Hell and status as fortunate or wretched have been written, prompting the question whether people should then rely on fate.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r1.anchor: ما من نفس منفوسة إلا كتب مكانها من الجنة والنار، وإلا قد كتبت شقية أو سعيدة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r2.claim: In a fuller version, the Prophet says the fortunate are enabled toward fortunate deeds and the wretched toward wretched deeds, then recites the two paths.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r2.anchor: أما أهل السعادة فييسرون لعمل أهل السعادة، وأما أهل الشقاء فييسرون إلى عمل أهل الشقاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r3.claim: Umar asks whether human deeds are already decreed; the Prophet says each person is facilitated, with the fortunate working toward happiness and the wretched toward misery. Tirmidhi grades the report hasan sahih.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r3.anchor: قال عمر: يا رسول الله، أرأيت ما نعمل فيه؟ أفي أمر قد فرغ أو مبتدأ أو مبتدع؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r4.claim: Jabir asks whether deeds concern a settled matter or a new one; the Prophet says the matter is settled, and tells Suraqah that every worker is facilitated for his work.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p418/r4.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله أنه قال: يا رسول الله، أنعمل لأمر قد فرغ منه، أو لأمر نستأنفه؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r1.claim: Muslim also transmits the report in which the Prophet says every worker is facilitated for the work for which he was created.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r1.anchor: ورواه مسلم عن أبي الطاهر، عن ابن وهب، به (1)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r2.claim: Two young men ask whether deeds follow what is written; the Prophet says to act, since everyone is facilitated for the work he was created to do.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r2.anchor: عن بشير (2) بن كعب العدوي قال: سأل غلامان شابان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالا يا رسول الله، أنعمل فيما جفت به الأقلام وجرت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r3.claim: The Prophet tells Abu al-Darda that each person is prepared for what he was created for; Ibn Kathir says Ahmad alone transmits this route.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419/r3.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قالوا: يا رسول الله، أرأيت ما نعمل، أمر قد فرغ منه أم شيء نستأنفه؟

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas relates that a palm owner repeatedly snatched fruit from poor children in a neighbor's house; the Prophet offered him a palm in Paradise, but he refused, so another man exchanged forty palms for it and donated it to the family.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r1.anchor: أن رجلا كان له نخل، ومنها نخلة فرعها إلى (7) دار رجل صالح فقير ذي عيال،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the story of the palm and the charitable buyer occasioned the revelation of the surah's opening through its contrast between giving and withholding.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p419#2/r2.anchor: قال عكرمة: قال ابن عباس: فأنزل الله عز وجل: {والليل إذا يغشى} إلى قوله:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the palm-story report transmitted by Ibn Abi Hatim very unusual.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p420/r1.anchor: هكذا رواه ابن أبي حاتم، وهو حديث غريب جدا.

JISHUMI:v10p7439/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r8.claim: Al-ʿusrā is the greatest affliction, opposite of ease; taysīr's opposite makes a matter difficult.
JISHUMI:v10p7439/r8.anchor: والعسرى: البلية العظمى، وهي تأنيث الأعسر، وأصله العسر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r2.claim: Making the person easy for hardship means abandoning and withholding divine assistance until obedience is hardest; alternatively, good and evil paths are named for their outcomes, or they are Paradise and Hell's roads in the afterlife.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r2.anchor: { فسنيسره للعسرى } فسنخذله ونمنعه الألطاف ، حتى تكون الطاعة أعسر شيء عليه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.claim: One report says these verses concern Abu Bakr and Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767/r3.anchor: وقيل : نزلتا في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه ، وفي أبي سفيان بن حرب

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r35.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r35.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r35.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets being eased toward hardship as being eased toward evil by God.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r35.anchor: للشر من الله تعالى , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r36.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r36.speaker: ابن مسعود
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r36.claim: Ibn Masud says the destination is the Fire.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r37.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r37.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r37.claim: Mawardi allows that God makes the means of goodness and righteousness difficult until doing them is hard.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r37.anchor: فسنعسر عليه أسباب الخير والصلاح حتى يصعب عليه فعلها

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.speaker: أبو الدرداء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.claim: Qatada reports from Khulayd, from Abu al-Darda, that the Prophet said two angels call each sunrise for God to replace the spender's gift and ruin the hoarder's wealth, then recited these verses; no grading is stated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p286/r38.anchor: يروي قتادة عن خليد عن أبي الدرداء أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( ما من يوم طلعت فيه شمسه إلا وملكان يناديان : اللهم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r1.claim: God eases him toward a disposition leading to the Fire, making obedience his hardest task.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r1.anchor: للخلة المؤدية إلى النار فتكون الطاعة أعسرشئ عليه واشدا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r2.claim: The good path is called easy because its outcome is ease, while the evil path is called hard because its outcome is hardship.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r2.anchor: سمى طريقة الخير باليسرى لأن عاقبتها اليسرى وطريقة الشر بالعسرى لأن عاقبتها العسر

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r3.claim: Alternatively, the easy and hard paths are the paths to Paradise and Hell.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#11/r3.anchor: أو أراد بهما طريقى الجنه والنار

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.speaker: علي عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.claim: At a funeral in Baqiʿ, the Prophet says each soul's destination is written, but people must act; each person is made ready for the work of the blessed or wretched, then he recites these verses.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r1.anchor: ما من نفس منفوسة إلا قد كتب مدخلها

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.speaker: علي عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.claim: Al-Tirmidhi's wording is graded hasan sahih; the Prophet repeats that everyone is made easy for the work for which they were created.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r2.anchor: بل اعملوا فكل ميسر أما من كان من أهل السعادة فإنه ييسر لعمل السعادة

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.speaker: غلامان شابان عن النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.claim: Two young men ask whether deeds follow prior decrees or begin anew; the Prophet says decrees, then tells them to act because each is enabled for the work assigned to him.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r3.anchor: «بل فيما جفت به الأقلام، وجرت به المقادير» قالا: ففيم العمل

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.speaker: الغلامان
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r4.claim: After hearing that each is made easy for the work for which he was created, the young men say they will strive and work.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r6.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r6.claim: He explains that God will prevent the miser from believing in God and His Messenger.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r6.anchor: سوف أحول بينه وبين الإيمان بالله وبرسوله

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r11.speaker: author وابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r11.claim: Yassiruhu means God makes the person's path easy toward evil; al-ʿusrā means evil or, in Ibn Masud's view, the Fire.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r11.anchor: { فسنيسره } أي نسهل طريقه. { للعسرى } أي للشر. وعن ابن مسعود: للنار.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r12.claim: Another explanation says God makes the causes of goodness and soundness difficult for him, so doing them becomes hard; this follows the earlier report of angels calling morning and evening.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:8-10/r12.anchor: فسنعسر عليه أسباب الخير والصلاح حتى يصعب عليه فعلها

QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r1.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r1.claim: Abu al-Darda reports a prayer that God replace the spender's gift and ruin the miser's withholding.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r1.anchor: وأعط ممسكا تلفا " رواه أبو الدرداء.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r2.claim: Qur'anic commands to spend establish generosity as a noble trait and miserliness as a base one.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r2.anchor: قال العلماء: ثبت بهذه الآية وبقوله:

QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r3.claim: Generosity means giving where giving is due; miserliness means withholding where giving is due, judged by resulting praise, blame, reward, or punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r3.anchor: وليس الجواد الذي يعطي في غير موضع العطاء، ولا البخيل الذي يمنع في موضع المنع،

QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r4.claim: Giving that earns neither reward nor praise but merits blame is wasteful, and its spenders are the brothers of devils subject to legal restraint.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r4.anchor: وهو من المبذرين الذين جعلهم الله إخوان الشياطين، وأوجب الحجر عليهم.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r5.claim: Withholding that merits praise rather than blame or punishment marks prudent people fit to manage others' property.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r5.anchor: فهو من أهل الرشد، الذين يستحقون القيام على أموال غيرهم، بحسن تدبيرهم

QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r6.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r6.claim: Al-Farra answers the objection that adversity cannot be made easy by comparing it with the idiom of announcing painful punishment as good news.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r6.anchor: الرابعة: قال الفراء: يقول القائل: كيف قال: «فسنيسره للعسرى»؟ وهل في العسرى تيسير؟

QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r7.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r7.claim: Al-Farra says taysir here means preparing or making ready, as Arabs say livestock has been made ready when it gives birth or approaches birth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r7.anchor: وقوله تعالى: { فسنيسره }: سنهيئه. والعرب تقول: قد يسرت الغنم: إذا ولدت

QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r8.claim: A cited poem uses yassarat for sheep becoming ready to give birth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:10/r8.anchor: هما سيدانا يزعمان وإنما يسوداننا أن يسرت غنماهما

QUTB-ZILAL:92:10/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:10/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:10/r1.claim: The rejecting person deserves to have everything made difficult: God enables hardship, denies ease, and makes each step distressing and further from right guidance.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:10/r1.anchor: ويستحق أن يعسر الله عليه كل شيء ، فييسره للعسرى ! ويوفقه إلى كل وعورة

QUTB-ZILAL:92:10/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:10/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:10/r2.claim: Repeated stumbles can carry a person farther into misery and away from God’s approval even while that person imagines success.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:10/r2.anchor: وإن حسب أنه سائر في طريق الفلاح . وإنما هو يعثر فيتقي العثار بعثرة أخرى

RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.claim: The passage explains that the differing human paths end in praiseworthy or blameworthy outcomes, reward or punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v31p180#2/r1.anchor: بين معنى اختلاف الأعمال فيما قلناه من العاقبة المحمودة والمذمومة

RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r1.claim: Al-yusra can mean Paradise, goodness, ease in all required acts and omissions, or renewed return to obedience; al-usra can mean shirk, hardship, or returning to withholding financial rights. Al-Qaffal explains both by their outcomes: obedience yields ease and sin hardship.
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r1.anchor: فكل ما أدت عاقبته إلى يسر وراحة وأمور محمودة ، فإن ذلك من اليسرى

RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r2.claim: The feminine ending may refer to a group of deeds, a feminine noun such as khilla or faʿla, the return to a prior act, or a feminine 'way'; it may also call Paradise easy because its promise makes difficult worship feel easy.
RAZI-FULL:v31p181/r2.anchor: أن المراد من اليسرى والعسرى إن كان جماعة الأعمال

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet taught each person's destination is recorded, then urged action because everyone is eased toward what they were created for; he recited these verses.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r1.anchor: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib related that the Prophet said, “There is no one among you except that his place is registered

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r11.claim: Turning away in disobedience brings reciprocity just as turning to God in repentance does; many gloss hardship as evil.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r11.anchor: Just as there is reciprocity when turning to God in repentance, so too there is reciprocity when turning away from God in disobedience. Hardship is glossed by many with “evil”

STUDYQURAN:92:5/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r12.claim: Disbelief and evil deeds can open the way to further evil until returning becomes harder, as the different natures of good and evil deeds in verse 4 imply.
STUDYQURAN:92:5/r12.anchor: when people disbelieve and commit evil deeds, God opens the way for them to commit further evil and it becomes increasingly difficult to turn back

TAB:92:10/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:10/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:10/r1.claim: God prepares the miser for the hard course in this life: deeds He dislikes and does not approve.
TAB:92:10/r1.anchor: فسنهيئه في الدنيا للخَلّة العُسرى ،   وهو من قولهم :  قد يسرت غنم فلان :  إذا ولدت وتهيأت للولادة

TAB:92:10/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:10/r2.speaker: author
TAB:92:10/r2.claim: The verb يسرت can describe a sheep giving birth or becoming ready to give birth; a cited poem uses the same form.
TAB:92:10/r2.anchor: قد يسرت غنم فلان :  إذا ولدت وتهيأت للولادة ،   وكما قال الشاعر :  هُمَا سَيّدَانا يَزْعُمانِ وإنّمَا *** يَسُودَانِنا أنْ يَسّرَتْ غَنَماهُمَا

TAB:92:10/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:10/r3.speaker: author
TAB:92:10/r3.claim: Although al-ʿusrā names hardship, paired statements allow God to make both the good path and the evil path easy for their respective people.
TAB:92:10/r3.anchor: وإذا جمع بين كلامين أحدهما ذكر الخير والاَخر ذكر الشرّ ،   جاز ذلك بالتيسير فيهما جميعا

TAB:92:10/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:10/r4.speaker: علي
TAB:92:10/r4.claim: The Prophet teaches that each person's place in Paradise or the Fire is written, yet people must act because each is made easy for their destined course; he recites these verses.
TAB:92:10/r4.anchor: ما مِنْكمْ مِنْ أحَدٍ إلاّ وَقَدْ كُتِبَ مَقْعَدُهُ مِنَ الجَنّةِ وَمَقْعَدُهُ مِنَ النّارِ

TAB:92:10/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:10/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB:92:10/r5.claim: In another report, a Bedouin asks why strive if destiny is settled; the Prophet says each is enabled for what they were created for, toward good or evil.
TAB:92:10/r5.anchor: قال النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم :  «كُلّ مُيَسّرٌ لِمَا خُلِقَ لَهُ ،   فَمَنْ يُرِدِ اللّهُ بِهِ خَيرا يَسّرَهُ لِسَبِيلِ الخَيرِ

TAB:92:10/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:10/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
TAB:92:10/r6.claim: When someone asks about work after the verse that everything was created by measure, the Prophet answers that each person is enabled for the easy or difficult path.
TAB:92:10/r6.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السّلَميّ ،   قال :  لما نزلت هذه الاَية :  إنّا كُلّ شَيْءٍ خَلَقْناهُ بِقَدَرٍ قال رجل :  يا رسول الله ،   ففيم العمل ؟

TAB:92:10/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:10/r7.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
TAB:92:10/r7.claim: Jābir reports the Prophet answering that every worker is enabled for that worker's own deed.
TAB:92:10/r7.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله أنه قال :  يا رسول الله ،   أنعمل لأمر قد فُرغ منه ،   أو لأمر نأتنفه ؟  فقال صلى الله عليه وسلم :  «كُلّ عامِلٍ مُيَسّرٌ لِعَمَلِهِ »

TAB:92:10/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:10/r8.speaker: بشير بن كعب
TAB:92:10/r8.claim: Bishr b. Kaʿb reports two young men asking whether they act according to decrees already written; the Prophet says to work, since each is enabled for the deed for which they were created.
TAB:92:10/r8.anchor: عن بشير بن كعب ،   قال :  سأل غلامان شابان النبيّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ،   فقالا :  يا رسول الله ،   أنعمل فيما جفّت به الأقلام

TAB:92:10/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:10/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:92:10/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses being made easy for the difficult course as being directed toward evil by God.
TAB:92:10/r9.anchor: عن عكرِمة ،   عن ابن عباس فَسَنُيَسّرُهُ لِلْعُسْرَى :  للشرّ من الله

TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ عن أبي الدرداء
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.claim: The Prophet says angels pray each day for God to replace what a spender gives and ruin what a miser withholds; the passage was revealed in connection with this.
TAB-FULL:v24p465/r3.anchor: اللهم أعط منفقا خلفا، وأعط ممسكا تلفا

TAB-FULL:v24p470/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r1.claim: God prepares the denier for the harder course: acting in ways He dislikes and does not approve.
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r1.anchor: والعسرى التي أخبر الله جل ثناؤه أنه ييسره لها: العمل بما يكرهه ولا يرضاه

TAB-FULL:v24p470/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r2.claim: The verb yassara can describe sheep made ready for birth; the “harder” phrase parallels the earlier easing for the easier path even without an expressed preposition.
TAB-FULL:v24p470/r2.anchor: قد يسرت غنم فلان: إذا ولدت وتهيأت للولادة

TAB-FULL:v24p473/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r1.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p473/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses being made ready for the harder path as being made ready for evil by God.

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.claim: The opposition between ease and hardship parallels 94:5–6, while the promise in 87:8 addresses the messenger.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:7-10:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Vgl. die Entgegensetzung von ʿusr und yusr in 94:5.6 sowie die wie 94:5.6 an den Verkünder gerichtete Verheißung 87:8

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.claim: The first antithesis pairs virtue and vice catalogues with promises of their eschatological outcomes; first-person plural marks these promises as God's speech and authorizes them alongside the oath.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r2.anchor: Diese Ankündigungen stehen in der ersten Person Plural, sind also eindeutig als Gottesrede markiert – ein Mittel literarischer Autorisierung

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r3.claim: The destinations are initially veiled through the near-homophonous opposites yusr and ʿusr combined with yassara, making the damned person's promised ease rhetorically paradoxical.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r3.anchor: Paradies und Hölle werden dabei vorerst nicht explizit benannt, sondern durch ein – bereits in 94:5.6 begegnendes – Wortspiel mit den nur in einem einzigen Konsonanten unterschiedenen

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.claim: The first stanza is symmetrical, with matching behavior-to-consequence sequences and a cross-rhyme produced by vowel variation, as Neuwirth observes.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r4.anchor: Die symmetrische Binnengliederung des Gesätzes in eine zweimalige Durchführung des Schemas ‚diesseitiges Verhalten – jenseitige Konsequenz’ unterstreicht ein durch Vokalvariation erzielter Kreuzreimeffekt

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.claim: The two halves are linked by paired terms: giving versus stinginess, piety versus self-sufficiency, affirmation versus denial, and ease versus hardship.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r5.anchor: V. 5 und 8 sind durch die Verwendung von Antonymen aufeinander bezogen: ʾaʿtā, „geben“ vs. baḫila, „geizen“, ittaqā, „gottesfürchtig sein“ vs. istaġnā

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.claim: Neuwirth classifies verse 11 with the theological predication in verses 12–13 rather than with the preceding description of the wicked.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.anchor: anders Neuwirth, Studien, 229 und Neuwirth, Frühmekkanische Suren, 228

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.claim: The final stanza reverses the earlier order of saved and damned; the outer blessed sections are linked by ittaqā in verse 5 and ʾatqā in verse 17.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r1.anchor: Zum einen wird die Reihenfolge Seliger – Verdammter (V. 5–7 und V. 8–11) jetzt invertiert (V. 14–16 Verdammter, V. 17–20 Seliger)

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.claim: The stanza halves mirror one another: earlier behavior lists precede reward or warning, while the final warning and promise precede each group's worldly conduct.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r2.anchor: In V. 5–7 und V. 8–11 ging zunächst ein Tugend- bzw. Lasterkatalog voraus, auf den dann jeweils ein Drohwort bzw. eine Verheißung folgten

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:14-21:kommentar/r3.claim: The second antithesis concretizes the first: verse 14 resolves the enigmatic threat of verse 10 as the image of blazing Hell.

TABATABAI:92:8-13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r2.claim: Being made ready for difficulty means being denied success in good works through their burden and an unwelcoming heart toward faith, or being prepared for punishment.
TABATABAI:92:8-13/r2.anchor: بتيسيره للعسرى خذلانه بعدم توفيقه للأعمال الصالحة

THALABI:v10p217/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p217/r7.claim: The miser withholds good spending, acts as if independent of God and denies the promised good; God then turns him toward disapproved deeds and punishment, with al-ʿusrā also understood as Hell itself.
THALABI:v10p217/r7.anchor: وأما من بخل بالنفقة في الخير واستغنى عن ربه فلم يرغب في ثوابه وكذب بالحسنى

THALABI:v10p217/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p217/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p217/r8.claim: Though facilitating someone toward hardship seems paradoxical, two opposing outcomes may be paired rhetorically, as in the phrase 'give them glad tidings of painful punishment.'
THALABI:v10p217/r8.anchor: فإن قيل: فأي تيسير في العسرى؟ قيل: إذا جمع بين كلامين أحدهما ذكر الخير والآخر ذكر الشر جاز ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81#2/r1.speaker: عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81#2/r1.claim: For the person identified as Umayya ibn Khalaf, God will prevent him from believing in God and affirming His messenger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81#2/r1.anchor: قال عطاء: يريد سوف أحول بينه وبين أن يؤمن بالله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81#2/r2.claim: He will find it difficult to give anything good.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p81#2/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يعسر عليه أن يعطي خيرا (¬8)

WAHIDI-QT:92:10/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:10/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:10/r1.claim: God abandons him until he does what leads to punishment and hardship.
WAHIDI-QT:92:10/r1.anchor: أي نخذله حتى يعمل بما يؤديه إلى العذاب والأمر العسير

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:10-19/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:10-19/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:10-19/r1.claim: God abandons him to works that lead to punishment and a difficult end.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:92:10-19/r1.anchor: { فسنيسره للعسرى } أي: نخذله حتى يعمل بما يؤديه إلى العذاب والأمر العسير.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r5.claim: Ease and hardship may occur in this life or the next, both of which belong to God; people should therefore follow what He commands.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r5.anchor: التيسير والتعسير إما أن يكونا في الدنيا أو في الآخرة ولله الآخرة والأولى

ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r8.claim: God prepares the denier for the hardest end, such as entering the Fire; he cannot overcome the hardship, which overwhelms him.
ELMALILI:92:5-11#2/r8.anchor: girmek gibi en zor ve en güç âkıbete götüren yola müyesser kılacağız

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r2.claim: The phrase is generally understood as “We prepare him for the hardest.”
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r2.anchor: Bu sebeple cümle genellikle “Biz onu en zora hazırlarız” şeklinde anlaşılmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r3.claim: God's preparing someone for hardship means withdrawing guidance and help after their refusal of God's and the Prophet's way and persistence in wrongdoing, here miserliness, leaving them to themselves.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r3.anchor: Allah’ın kulunu zor olana hazırlamasından maksat da kulun, Allah ve resulünün gösterdiği yolu kabul etmeyerek yanlışlarda ısrar etmesi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r4.claim: Left to himself, a person pursues desire without regard to lawful limits, finds sin easy and pleasurable, ends in Hell, and cannot ransom himself with accumulated wealth (5:36; 70:11–16).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:8/r4.anchor: kendi başına kalan kul helâl haram demeden nefsânî arzularını tatmine çalışır; kötülük yapmak, günah işlemek ona kolay gelir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.claim: An alternative contextual account identifies the giver as Abu al-Dahdah and the miser as the Ansari palm owner; it maps ease to Paradise, hardship to Hell, and death to loss of wealth.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:21/r1.anchor: { فأما من أعطى واتقى } يعني أبا الدحداح. { وصدق بالحسنى } أي بالثواب

THALABI:v10p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r1.speaker: عطاء
THALABI:v10p220/r1.claim: A man refused the Prophet’s offer of a date palm in Paradise for his palm that dropped fruit into a neighbor’s yard; Abū al-Daḥdāḥ bought and donated it, and the Prophet transferred it to the neighbor. The account identifies them with the surah’s contrasting figures.
THALABI:v10p220/r1.anchor: عطاء قال: كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة، وكان له جار، فكان يسقط من بلحها في دار جاره

THALABI:v10p220/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p220/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p220/r3.claim: The palm’s owner represents the miser who deems himself self-sufficient and denies reward; he is eased toward Hell and is the “most wretched” who enters the blazing fire.
THALABI:v10p220/r3.anchor: وأما من بخل واستغنى يعني الأنصاري وكذب بالحسنى يعني الثواب فسنيسره للعسرى يعني النار

ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r2.claim: Al-ʿusrā is the bad and difficult condition in this world and the next.
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r2.anchor: { للعسرى } ، وهي الحالة السيئة في الدنيا والآخرة .

ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says God abandons the miser and withholds grace until obedience becomes hardest, citing the constricted heart; the author flags this opening explanation as Muʿtazilī.
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : فسنخذله ونمنعه الألطاف حتى تكون الطاعة أعسر شيء عليه وأشد كقوله : { يجعل صدره ضيقاً حرجاً كأنما يصعد في السماء }

ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī alternatively says the paths are named for their outcomes, ease and hardship, or means the paths to Paradise and Hell in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r4.anchor: إذ سمى طريقة الخير باليسرى لأن عاقبتها اليسر ، وطريقة الشر العسرى لأن عاقبتها العسر ، أو أراد بهما طريقي الجنة والنار

ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:8/r5.claim: The author marks al-Zamakhsharī’s account of withholding divine grace as carrying a Muʿtazilī insinuation.

ABUHAYYAN:92:10/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:10/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:10/r1.claim: The phrase mirrors the earlier “make him easy for ease”; since hardship is not ease, taysīr here means preparation, possible for either outcome.
ABUHAYYAN:92:10/r1.anchor: وجاء { فسنيسره للعسرى } على سبيل المقابلة لقوله : { فسنيسره لليسرى } ، والعسرى لا تيسير فيها ، وقد يراد بالتيسير التهيئة

ALUSI:92:10/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r1.claim: God readies him for a disposition leading to hardship, such as entering Hell and its preliminaries; al-ʿusrā is formed analogously to al-yusrā.
ALUSI:92:10/r1.anchor: أي للخصلة المؤدية إلى العسر والشدة كدخول النار ومباديه ووصفها بالعسرى

ALUSI:92:10/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r2.claim: Though taysīr derives from ease, here it means preparing and readying for what brings ease or hardship.
ALUSI:92:10/r2.anchor: وأصل التيسير من اليسر بمعنى السهولة لكن أريد التهيئة والإعداد للأمر

ALUSI:92:10/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r3.claim: The future particle may add emphasis or indicate the magnitude and delayed realization of the promised next-world recompense.
ALUSI:92:10/r3.anchor: والسين في سنيسره قيل للتأكيد وقيل للدلالة على أن لحزاء الموعود معظمة

ALUSI:92:10/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r4.claim: The sequence of withholding, self-sufficiency, and denial follows the explanation already given.
ALUSI:92:10/r4.anchor: وتقديم البخل فالاستغناء فالتكذيب يعلم وجهه مما تقدم

ALUSI:92:10/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r6.claim: One interpretation makes the outcomes obedience: God grants لطف and success toward obedience for the giver, and withdraws enabling graces so obedience becomes hardest for the miser, related to 6:125.
ALUSI:92:10/r6.anchor: وقيل التيسير أولاً بمعنى اللطف وثانياً بمعنى الخذلان واليسرى والعسرى الطاعة

ALUSI:92:10/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r7.claim: Another view takes al-yusrā and al-ʿusrā as the paths to Paradise and Hell and taysīr as guidance, a promise and threat concerning the afterlife.
ALUSI:92:10/r7.anchor: وجوز أن يراد باليسرى طريق الجنة وبالعسرى طريق النار وبالتيسير في الموضعين معنى الهداية

ALUSI:92:10/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r8.claim: Al-Alūsī considers it sound and near that taysīr means preparation and the outcomes are obedience and disobedience together with their good or blameworthy dispositions.
ALUSI:92:10/r8.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بالتيسير التهيئة والإعداد واليسرى والعسرى الطاعة والمعصية ومباديهما

ALUSI:92:10/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r9.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
ALUSI:92:10/r9.claim: In a report from ʿAlī, the Prophet says each person's seats in Paradise and Hell are written; when asked whether to rely on this, he commands action, saying each is made easy for the deeds suited to their created end, and recites 92:5–7.
ALUSI:92:10/r9.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة

ALUSI:92:10/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:10/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:10/r10.claim: The Prophet's command to work means fulfill servanthood and the purpose of creation, while leaving hidden matters of divine lordship to God.
ALUSI:92:10/r10.anchor: عليكم بشأن العبودية وما خلقتم لأجله وأمرتم به وكلوا أمور الربوبية المغيبة

BAGHAWI:92:10/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:10/r1.claim: God prepares the denier for evil, letting him perform what displeases God until he deserves the Fire.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r1.anchor: سنهيئه للشر بأن نجريه على يديه حتى يعمل بما لا يرضي الله ،   فيستوجب به النار

BAGHAWI:92:10/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r2.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI:92:10/r2.claim: Muqatil says God makes it difficult for the person to do good.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل : نعسر عليه أن يأتي خيراً

BAGHAWI:92:10/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r3.speaker: علي
BAGHAWI:92:10/r3.claim: Ali reports the Prophet saying every soul's destination is recorded, but people must still act: each is facilitated for the deeds of the blessed or wretched, and the Prophet recited these verses.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r3.anchor: وروينا عن علي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : " ما من نفس منفوسة إلا كتب الله

BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.claim: An anonymous report says the passage was revealed about Abu Bakr buying Bilal from Umayya ibn Khalaf for a garment and ten coins and freeing him; their opposed efforts are contrasted.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r4.anchor: قيل : نزلت في أبي بكر الصديق اشترى بلالاً من أمية ابن خلف ببردة وعشرة أوراق ،   فأعتقه

BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.speaker: عطاء
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.claim: Ata recounts an Ansari's palm tree whose fallen dates entered a neighbor's home; the Prophet offered a tree in Paradise, the owner refused, and Abu al-Dahdah bought it with his garden and gave it to the neighbor. The report maps the giver to Abu al-Dahdah and the miser to the Ansari.
BAGHAWI:92:10/r5.anchor: عن عطاء ،   قال : " كان لرجل من الأنصار نخلة وكان له جار يسقط من بلحها في داره

BAYDAWI:92:10/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:10/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:10/r1.claim: God prepares him for a disposition leading to hardship and distress, such as entry into the Fire.
BAYDAWI:92:10/r1.anchor: للخلة المؤدية إلى العسر والشدة كدخول النار

BIQAI:92:10/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:10/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:10/r1.claim: Because the denier is fixed on sensible things like livestock, God prepares him for the most difficult, most adverse course.
BIQAI:92:10/r1.anchor: ولما كان جامداً مع المحسوسات كالبهائم

BIQAI:92:10/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:10/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:10/r2.claim: Al-ʿusrā is the hardest and most distressing trait: doing what angers God, which leads to Hell and to its causes.
BIQAI:92:10/r2.anchor: أي للخصلة التي هي أعسر الأشياء وأنكدها

BIQAI:92:10/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:10/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:10/r3.claim: The majestic plural used for both paths signals how remote taking either path is: good is ringed by hardship, while reason and original nature restrain evil.
BIQAI:92:10/r3.anchor: وأشار بنون العظمة في كل من نجد الخير ونجد الشر

BIQAI:92:10/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:10/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:10/r4.claim: The matter was settled in eternity through the designation of the blessed and the wretched; the author invokes the Prophetic saying that each person is facilitated toward what he was created for.
BIQAI:92:10/r4.anchor: وذلك كله أمر قد فرغ منه في الأزل بتعيين أهل السعادة وأهل الشقاوة

BIQAI:92:10/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:10/r5.speaker: رسول الله
BIQAI:92:10/r5.claim: The Prophet says that each person is facilitated toward what he was created for; the author cites this as a summary of the preceding decree.
BIQAI:92:10/r5.anchor: وكل كما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم - ميسر لما خلق له

DURR:92:4/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:4/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
DURR:92:4/r3.claim: Ibn Masud reports that Abu Bakr bought and freed Bilal, and that the revelation contrasts Abu Bakr's effort with that of Umayya and Ubayy, identifying faith in the good as monotheism and the hard outcome as Hell.
DURR:92:4/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أن أبا بكر الصديق اشترى بلالاً من أمية بن خلف وأبي بن خلف ببردة وعشر أواق

DURR:92:5/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:5/r4.claim: In the report through ʿIkrima, Ibn Abbas says the miser denies God's recompense and God makes him easy for evil.
DURR:92:5/r4.anchor: من طريق عكرمة عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى } من الفضل { واتقى } قال : اتقى ربه

DURR:92:5/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:92:5/r13.claim: In a report through al-Kalbi and Abu Salih, Ibn Abbas identifies the giver as Abu Bakr and the miser who denies the good as Abu Sufyan ibn Harb.
DURR:92:5/r13.anchor: في طريق الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس في قوله : { فأما من أعطى واتقى وصدق بالحسنى فسنيسره لليسرى } قال : أبو بكر الصديق

DURR:92:5/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r14.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
DURR:92:5/r14.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise and Hell is written, yet commanded action: people are facilitated toward deeds of felicity or misery, then he recited these verses.
DURR:92:5/r14.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب قال : «كنا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في جنازة فقال : ما منكم من أحد إلا وقد كتب مقعده من الجنة ومقعده من النار

DURR:92:5/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:5/r15.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
DURR:92:5/r15.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami reports that after 54:49 was revealed, a man asked whether deeds were newly begun or already decreed; the Prophet replied to act, since each is facilitated toward ease or hardship.
DURR:92:5/r15.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن السلمي قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية { إنا كل شيء خلقناه بقدر } [ القمر : 49 ] قال رجل : يا رسول الله ففيم العمل
