DURR:92:17/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:92:17/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR:92:17/r2.claim: Asked whether deeds concern fixed decrees or future action, the Prophet says destiny is fixed but commands people to act, since each is eased for what they were created for; he recites 92:5–10.
DURR:92:17/r2.anchor: قال سراقة : ففيم العمل إذن يا رسول الله ؟ قال : اعملوا فكل ميسر لما خلق له

IBNASHUR:92:10/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r1.claim: Taysīr is making something easy to obtain; its object is what is made easy, while the following lām names the beneficiary who benefits from the easing.

IBNASHUR:92:10/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r2.claim: The complement with lām names the person for whose sake something difficult is eased and who benefits from its ease; the author compares this construction with Q 20:26 and 54:17.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r2.anchor: والمجرور باللام بعده هو الذي يسهَّل الشيء الصعب لأجله وهو الذي ينتفع بسهولة الأمر

IBNASHUR:92:10/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r3.claim: Al-yusrā means what entails no hardship; its feminine form can denote a blissful condition in the Hereafter or a place.

IBNASHUR:92:10/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم ومجاهد
IBNASHUR:92:10/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam and Mujahid interpret al-yusrā as Paradise.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r4.anchor: وقد فسرت اليسرى بالجنة عن زيد بن أسلم ومجاهد

IBNASHUR:92:10/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r5.claim: The word may broadly include what benefits its possessor without hardship, namely what suits him.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r5.anchor: الذي لا يشق على صاحبه ، أي الملائم

IBNASHUR:92:10/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r6.claim: Al-ʿusrā may mean the difficult state and punishment, or Hell as the place of hardship; deeds can also be described by their eventual outcome.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r6.anchor: لأنها مكان العسر والشدائد على أهلها

IBNASHUR:92:10/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r7.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR:92:10/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains facilitation as gradually involving each person in deeds of felicity or misery; deeds are called easy or hard by their eventual outcome.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r7.anchor: في عملي السعادة والشقاوة وبه فسر ابن عطية

IBNASHUR:92:10/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r8.claim: On this reading, the future marker indicates continuing facilitation from now until life's end, as in Joseph 12:98.

IBNASHUR:92:10/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r9.claim: The definite article in al-yusrā and al-ʿusrā can mark a generic class or a previously specified referent, depending on the interpretation.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r9.anchor: لتعريف الجنس أو للعهد على اختلاف المعاني

IBNASHUR:92:10/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r10.claim: One analysis reads the syntax as reversal: the person is made the object facilitated for al-yusrā or al-ʿusrā, intensifying the facilitation like the Arabic expression about presenting a she-camel to a watering-trough.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r10.anchor: بطريق القلب بأن يكون أصل الكلام

IBNASHUR:92:10/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r11.claim: A second analysis uses taysīr metaphorically for preparation, by the entailment between preparing something for an end and making it accessible; the lām gives purpose.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r11.anchor: في التهيئة والإعداد بعلاقة اللزوم بين إعداد الشيء للشيء وتيسره له

IBNASHUR:92:10/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r12.claim: On the preparation reading, al-yusrā and al-ʿusrā name Paradise and Hell, and the understood entry into each is hastened; making entry easy implies speed, as in Q 50:44.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r12.anchor: شأن الصعب الإبطاء وشأن السهل السرعة

IBNASHUR:92:10/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r13.claim: Calling the route to Hell al-ʿusrā on this reading is wordplay built on a mock-metaphor, signaled by al-ʿusrā.

IBNASHUR:92:10/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r14.claim: Because the prior acts of giving, piety, affirmation, miserliness, self-sufficiency, and denial precede the future facilitation, it concerns continuing and increasing those acts.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r14.anchor: والتيسير مستقبل بعد حصولها فهو تيسير

IBNASHUR:92:10/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r15.claim: A further permissible reading keeps taysīr literal, makes al-yusrā and al-ʿusrā descriptions of easy and difficult conditions, and understands facilitation as persistence in the deed.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r15.anchor: أن يجعل التيسير على حقيقته ويجعل اليسرى وصفا

IBNASHUR:92:10/r16.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r16.speaker: علي
IBNASHUR:92:10/r16.claim: ʿAlī reports that at a funeral in Baqīʿ al-Gharqad the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise and Hell was written, urged them to act because each is facilitated for what they were created for, and recited this passage.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r16.anchor: عن علي قال :   "  كنا مع رسول الله في بقيع الغرقد

IBNASHUR:92:10/r17.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r17.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r17.claim: In the hadith, a person's written place represents God's knowledge of the actual outcome, fixed without increase or decrease; it does not itself answer why people should act.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r17.anchor: جعلت الكتابة تمثيلا لعلم الله بالمعلومات علما موافقا لما سيكون

IBNASHUR:92:10/r18.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r18.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r18.claim: The hadith's answer is that righteous action signals a good end; mentioning its opposite completes the comparison but is not part of that answer.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r18.anchor: فائدة العمل الصالح أنه عنوان على العاقبة الحسنة

IBNASHUR:92:10/r19.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r19.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r19.claim: The hadith's facilitation means preparation for good or evil deeds, unlike the verse's usage; the Prophet's recitation connects the verse to his statement as explanation and evidence.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r19.anchor: في الحديث علق به عمل أهل السعادة فتعين أن يكون تيسيرا للعمل

IBNASHUR:92:10/r20.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r20.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r20.claim: The hadith can show that God facilitates servants toward felicity or misery, whether in foundational faith or disbelief and in further good deeds that increase felicity or reduce misery.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r20.anchor: أن يعمل بعمل السعادة أو عمل الشقاء سواء كان عمله أصلا للسعادة كالإيمان

IBNASHUR:92:10/r21.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r21.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r21.claim: Alternatively, the recitation supports the command to act: deeds mark divine facilitation, with al-yusrā signifying felicity and al-ʿusrā misery, culminating in Paradise or the Fire.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r21.anchor: لأن الآية ذكرت عملا وذكرت تيسيرا لليسرى وتيسيرا للعسرى

IBNASHUR:92:10/r22.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r22.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r22.claim: The passage distinguishes God's prior knowledge of human deeds from His revealed commands; a person's deeds through death indicate what God knew, while deeds remain the means to Paradise or Hell.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r22.anchor: وأن ما يصدر عن الناس من أعمال ظاهرة وباطنة إلى خاتمة كل أحد

IBNASHUR:92:10/r23.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r23.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r23.claim: Giving is singled out despite being included in piety, and miserliness despite self-sufficiency, to urge Muslims to give; these traits distinguish Muslims from polytheists.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r23.anchor: فالإعطاء والتقوى شعار المسلمين مع التصديق بالحسنى وضد الثلاثة من شعار المشركين

IBNASHUR:92:10/r24.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:10/r24.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:10/r24.claim: The verse uses combination with division and four antitheses: giving/miserliness, piety/self-sufficiency, affirming/denying, and al-yusrā/al-ʿusrā.
IBNASHUR:92:10/r24.anchor: محسن الجمع مع التقسيم ، ومحسن الطباق ، أربع مرات

IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Hell is recorded; when asked whether to rely on this, he said to act, since each is facilitated, then recited al-Layl 92:5–10.
IBNHIBBAN:335/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان في جنازة فأخذ عودا ينكت في الأرض

IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.claim: ʿAlī reports that the Prophet said each person's place in Paradise or Hell is recorded; when asked whether to rely on this, he said to act, since each is facilitated, then recited al-Layl 92:5–10.
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r1.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طالب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه كان في جنازة فأخذ عودا ينكت في الأرض

IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.author: Ibn Ḥibbān
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.speaker: شعبة
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.claim: Shuʿba adds that Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir also narrated the report to him, corroborating its transmission from Sulaymān al-Aʿmash.
IBNHIBBAN:v2p47#2/r2.anchor: قال شعبة حدثني منصور بن المعتمر فلم أنكره من حديث سليمان

IBNATIYYA:92:10/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:10/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:10/r1.claim: The commentary repeats its explanation of easing a person gradually into good deeds and a facilitation fixed in prior knowledge, although it quotes al-yusrā here.
IBNATIYYA:92:10/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { فسنيسره لليسرى } ومعناه : سيظهر تيسيرنا إياه يتدرج فيه من أعمال الخير

IBNATIYYA:92:10/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:10/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:10/r2.claim: The passage defines al-yusrā as a good, pleasing condition in this world and the next.
IBNATIYYA:92:10/r2.anchor: و «اليسرى » الحال الحسنة المرضية في الدنيا والآخرة .

IBNATIYYA:92:10/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:10/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:10/r3.claim: Al-ʿusrā is the bad condition in this world and the next.
IBNATIYYA:92:10/r3.anchor: و «العسرى » : الحال السيئة في الدنيا والآخرة .

IBNKATHIR:92:10/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:10/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:92:10/r1.claim: Al-ʿusrā means the path of evil; Ibn Kathir compares this divine turning of hearts to 6:110.
IBNKATHIR:92:10/r1.anchor: أي : لطريق الشر ،   كما قال تعالى : { وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ

KASHSHAF:92:10/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:10/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:10/r1.claim: One explanation is that God abandons him and withholds grace until obedience becomes his hardest and most difficult task.
KASHSHAF:92:10/r1.anchor: ونمنعه الألطاف ،   حتى تكون الطاعة أعسر شيء عليه وأشده

KASHSHAF:92:10/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:10/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:10/r2.claim: The easy path is named for the ease of its outcome, while the hard path is named for its difficult outcome.
KASHSHAF:92:10/r2.anchor: طريقة الخير باليسرى ،   لأن عاقبتها اليسر

KASHSHAF:92:10/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:10/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:10/r3.claim: Another explanation is that God will guide them in the afterlife to the two paths, Paradise and Hell.
KASHSHAF:92:10/r3.anchor: أو أراد بهما طريقي الجنة والنار

KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.claim: A report says these verses were revealed concerning Abū Bakr and Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb.
KASHSHAF:92:10/r4.anchor: نزلتا في أبي بكر رضي الله عنه

MAWARDI:92:10/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:10/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI:92:10/r1.anchor: أحدهما : للشر من الله تعالى ،   قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI:92:10/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:10/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:10/r3.claim: Māwardī also suggests that God makes the means to goodness and righteousness difficult until doing them is hard for the person.
MAWARDI:92:10/r3.anchor: فسنعسر عليه أسباب الخير والصلاح حتى يصعب عليه فعلها

MAWARDI:92:10/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:10/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI:92:10/r4.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reports from the Prophet, through Qatāda and Khulayd, that each sunrise two angels ask God to replace the giver and bring loss to the one who withholds; the Prophet then recites the giving passage and the following verse.
MAWARDI:92:10/r4.anchor: يروي قتادة عن خليد عن أبي الدرداء أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : " ما من يوم طلعت فيه شمسه إلا

NASAFI:92:10/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:10/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:10/r1.claim: God prepares him for the difficult course leading to Hell, making obedience his hardest and most burdensome task.
NASAFI:92:10/r1.anchor: { فَسَنُيَسّرُهُ للعسرى } للخلة المؤدية إلى النار فتكون الطاعة أعسر شيء عليه وأشد

NASAFI:92:10/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:10/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:10/r2.claim: Another explanation names the good path “easy” for its easy outcome, and the evil path “difficult” for its difficult outcome.
NASAFI:92:10/r2.anchor: أو سمى طريقة الخير باليسرى لأن عاقبتها اليسر

NASAFI:92:10/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:10/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:10/r3.claim: Alternatively, the easy and difficult ways are the paths to Paradise and Hell.
NASAFI:92:10/r3.anchor: أو أراد بهما طريقي الجنة والنار

QURTUBI:92:8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:8/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن الضحاك
QURTUBI:92:8/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas, as transmitted by al-Dahhak, explains the hard course as God preventing the person from believing in God and His Messenger.
QURTUBI:92:8/r2.anchor: روى الضحاك عن ابن عباس " فسنيسره للعسرى " قال : سوف أحول بينه

QURTUBI:92:10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:10/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:10/r1.claim: The phrase means that God will make the person's path easy.

QURTUBI:92:10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:10/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI:92:10/r3.claim: Ibn Masud interprets the hard course as the Fire.
QURTUBI:92:10/r3.anchor: أي للشر . وعن ابن مسعود : للنار

QURTUBI:92:10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:10/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:92:10/r4.claim: Another explanation is that God makes the causes of good and righteousness difficult for him, so acting on them becomes hard.
QURTUBI:92:10/r4.anchor: وقيل : أي فسنعسر عليه أسباب الخير والصلاح حتى يصعب عليه فعلها

QURTUBI:92:10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:10/r5.speaker: أبو الدرداء
QURTUBI:92:10/r5.claim: Al-Qurtubi recalls Abu al-Darda's report of angels calling morning and evening for recompense for the spender and loss for the miser.
QURTUBI:92:10/r5.anchor: وقد تقدم أن الملك ينادي صباحا ومساء : [ اللهم أعط منفقا خلفا ، وأعط ممسكا تلفا ] . رواه أبو الدرداء

QURTUBI:92:10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:10/r6.speaker: العلماء
QURTUBI:92:10/r6.claim: Scholars infer from this and other verses that generosity is a noble virtue and miserliness a vile one.
QURTUBI:92:10/r6.anchor: قال العلماء : ثبت بهذه الآية وبقوله

QURTUBI:92:10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:10/r7.claim: Generosity means giving where giving is proper; miserliness means withholding where giving is due, not giving indiscriminately or withholding where restraint is proper.
QURTUBI:92:10/r7.anchor: وليس الجواد الذي يعطي في غير موضع العطاء ، ولا البخيل الذي يمنع في موضع المنع ، لكن الجواد الذي يعطي في موضع العطاء

QURTUBI:92:10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:10/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:10/r8.claim: Giving that earns no reward or praise but merits blame is wasteful, not generosity; such spendthrifts are described as Satan's brothers and are subject to interdiction.
QURTUBI:92:10/r8.anchor: ومن لم يستفد بالعطاء أجرا ولا حمدا ، وإنما استوجب به ذما فليس بجواد

QURTUBI:92:10/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:10/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:10/r9.claim: A person whose withholding merits neither blame nor punishment but earns praise is rightly guided and fit to manage others' wealth because of sound judgment.
QURTUBI:92:10/r9.anchor: ومن لم يستوجب بالمنع عقابا ولا ذما ، واستوجب به حمدا ، فهو من أهل الرشد

QURTUBI:92:10/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:10/r10.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:92:10/r10.claim: Al-Farra answers the apparent paradox of making someone easy for hardship by analogy to giving glad tidings of painful punishment: paired good and evil statements use the same terms.
QURTUBI:92:10/r10.anchor: قال الفراء : يقول القائل : كيف قال : " فسنيسره للعسرى " ؟ وهل في العسرى تيسير ؟

QURTUBI:92:10/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:10/r11.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:92:10/r11.claim: Al-Farra glosses the verb as preparing someone; Arabs use it of sheep when they give birth or are ready to do so.
QURTUBI:92:10/r11.anchor: قال الفراء : وقوله تعالى : " فسنيسره " : سنهيئه . والعرب تقول : قد يسرت الغنم

QURTUBI:92:10/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:10/r12.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI:92:10/r12.claim: A cited poem uses the verb of ewes being ready to give birth, supporting al-Farra's explanation of preparing.
QURTUBI:92:10/r12.anchor: هما سيدانا يزعمان وإنما *** يسوداننا أن يسرت غنماهما

RAZI:92:10/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:10/r1.claim: God singles out the unbeliever for abandonment: sin becomes more likely than obedience, so one alternative must necessarily occur.
RAZI:92:10/r1.anchor: وقوله : { فسنيسره للعسرى } يدل على أنه خص الكافر بهذا الخذلان

RAZI:92:10/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r2.speaker: القفال
RAZI:92:10/r2.claim: Al-Qaffal reads this as a metaphor naming one opposite by the other: withholding graces prompting obedience is called facilitating hardship.
RAZI:92:10/r2.anchor: أجاب القفال رحمه الله عن وجه التمسك بالآية من وجوه ( أحدها ) : أن تسمية أحد الضدين باسم الآخر مجاز مشهور

RAZI:92:10/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r3.speaker: author
RAZI:92:10/r3.claim: Al-Razi reports al-Qaffal's alternative that the action is attributed to its cause, not its agent, as when idols are said to lead people astray.
RAZI:92:10/r3.anchor: سمى ترك هذه الألطاف تيسيرا للعسرى ( وثانيها ) : أن يكون ذلك على جهة إضافة الفعل إلى المسبب له دون الفاعل

RAZI:92:10/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:92:10/r4.claim: Al-Razi reports al-Qaffal's third reading: the wording is a divine judgment and report about the outcome.
RAZI:92:10/r4.anchor: وثالثها ) : أن يكون ذلك على سبيل الحكم به والإخبار عنه

RAZI:92:10/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:92:10/r5.claim: Al-Razi rejects the alternatives as departures from the apparent sense, which decisive reason confirms.
RAZI:92:10/r5.anchor: والجواب ) : عن الكل أنه عدول عن الظاهر ، وذلك غير جائز ، لاسيما أنا بينا أن الظاهر من جانبنا متأكد بالدليل العقلي القاطع

RAZI:92:10/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن علي عليه السلام
RAZI:92:10/r6.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet said God knows every soul's place in Paradise or Hell; asked whether to rely on that, he commanded them to act, since each is facilitated toward what it was created for.
RAZI:92:10/r6.anchor: روى عن علي عليه السلام عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : «ما من نفس منفوسة إلا وقد علم الله مكانها من الجنة والنار

RAZI:92:10/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r7.speaker: القفال
RAZI:92:10/r7.claim: Al-Qaffal answers that everyone was created to worship God, citing the statement that jinn and humans were created only to worship Him.
RAZI:92:10/r7.anchor: أجاب القفال عنه بأن الناس كلهم خلقوا ليعبدوا الله ، كما قال : { وما خلقت الجن والإنس إلا ليعبدون }

RAZI:92:10/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r8.speaker: author
RAZI:92:10/r8.claim: Al-Razi calls that answer weak: the Prophet's reply means act, since each is facilitated toward what accords with God's unchangeable knowledge.
RAZI:92:10/r8.anchor: واعلم أن هذا ضعيف لأنه عليه السلام إنما ذكر هذا جوابا عن سؤالهم ، يعني اعملوا فكل ميسر لما وافق معلوم الله

RAZI:92:10/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r9.speaker: author
RAZI:92:10/r9.claim: Al-Razi gives three readings of the future sīn: gentle enabling, future outcomes as conduct changes, or delay until afterlife reward arrives.
RAZI:92:10/r9.anchor: المسألة الخامسة : في دخول السين في قوله : { فسنيسره } وجوه

RAZI:92:10/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r10.speaker: author
RAZI:92:10/r10.claim: On the first reading, the sīn marks God's gentle, certain enabling; al-Razi compares it with the command to worship so people may become God-fearing.
RAZI:92:10/r10.anchor: أنه على سبيل الترفيق والتلطيف وهو من الله تعالى قطع ويقين ، كما في قوله : { اعبدوا ربكم } إلى قوله { لعلكم تتقون }

RAZI:92:10/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r11.speaker: author
RAZI:92:10/r11.claim: A second reading allows the obedient to become disobedient and sinners to repent into obedience, with the wording framed in the future.
RAZI:92:10/r11.anchor: أن يحمل ذلك على أن المطيع قد يصير عاصيا ، والعاصي قد يصير بالتوبة مطيعا

RAZI:92:10/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:10/r12.speaker: author
RAZI:92:10/r12.claim: Most reward comes in the afterlife, whose time is known only to God; the sīn therefore signals a delayed promise.
RAZI:92:10/r12.anchor: أن الثواب لما كان أكثره واقعا في الآخرة ، وكان ذلك مما لم يأت وقته ، ولا يقف أحد على وقته إلا الله
